title: Negative possession questions review
focus: Mix the forms and sentence patterns already taught in this pack.
targetSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions

exercises.prompt: Change “Teillä ei ole tyynyä.” (“You do not have a pillow.”) into “Don’t you have a pillow?” Use teillä ("you as owner") and tyynyä ("pillow"). Address a group.
exercises.explanation: Change the opening to eikö; keep the supplied possessor and noun form.
requiredSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.targetSkill: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: te has the learned possession form teillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
tyyny + -a = tyynyä. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

exercises.prompt: Ask and reply: “Don’t we have a dog? We do have it.” Use meillä ("we as owner") and koiraa ("dog"). Owner follows question word.
acceptedAnswers: Eikö meillä ole koiraa? Kyllä, on.
exercises.explanation: First form the question; then echo on to confirm possession or ei ole to deny it.
requiredSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
